tradition.name: Ambient lo-fi
tradition.lineage: Ambient with deliberately exposed recording grain and small repeated textures. A documented branch is Earthen Sea’s Tidal Range: environmental recordings are transformed into a quiet electronic space, with the release explicitly filed under both ambient and lo-fi. The chosen tape-coloured sampler and slow synthesizer bed model that branch; this does not establish all artists on a changing platform playlist as one historical movement.

extras.description: Low-fidelity ambience gives quiet environmental or sampled material and softly sustained harmony priority over a foreground beat. Earthen Sea’s Tidal Range provides a concrete ambient/lo-fi intersection rather than a claimed birthplace. Tape grain, muffled timbre and restrained repetition are the authored defaults. It differs from the existing lo-fi umbrella and lo-fi hip hop defaults by omitting a bass-and-drum groove ensemble; it differs from clean space ambient by allowing recording texture and short imperfect loops to remain audible.

entries.geo_rationale: Outlaw Ocean identifies Earthen Sea in Brooklyn; this locates the selected documented practitioner, not an origin for all ambient lo-fi.

equivalence.decision: No exact equivalent established; proposal retained for integration review.

tradition.name: Ambient trance
tradition.lineage: The atmospheric listening side of trance and related electronic music, represented by Carbon Based Lifeforms, Solar Fields and the Ultimae orbit. Long melodic layers and repeated sequencer/bass figures may carry soft beats or become beatless. The selected model retains a measured machine pulse rather than prescribing a peak-time trance build.

extras.description: Ambient trance is an atmospheric trance-adjacent listening category, spanning hypnotic electronic sequences, resonant bass and lingering melodic layers rather than only festival-speed four-on-the-floor anthems. The source-linked Sounds of Spotify list includes Carbon Based Lifeforms, Solar Fields, AES Dana and Union Jack. The default models a gently persistent synth/bass/drum pulse. Compared with classic or uplifting trance it recesses intensity and climactic song architecture; compared with beatless ambient it retains sequenced rhythmic recurrence. There is substantial overlap with existing ambient_psychill: this allocation is a broader discovery category, not an assertion of an unrelated lineage or a uniquely measured sonic boundary.
exemplars: Solar Fields — Until We Meet the Sky

tradition.name: Ambient worship
tradition.lineage: Contemporary Christian music for prayer and reflection that uses ambient soundscapes, intimate sung phrases and melodic acoustic or electronic layers. Salt of the Sound explicitly uses this name for a listening-oriented form alongside, rather than exclusively inside, congregational worship services.

extras.description: Ambient worship places Christian prayer, hymns and reflective sung phrases within expansive soundscapes. Salt of the Sound’s firsthand definition includes both large textures and soft intimate songs, with vocals in varying amounts, and distinguishes the style from a typical Sunday congregational set. Their release notes document muted piano and ethereal phrases as well as instrumental meditations. The default is the quiet vocal/piano/pad branch, not a claim that all releases use this exact trio. Compared with contemporary_worship, drums, massed congregation and the auditorium crescendo cease to be default chairs; compared with secular ambient, the reflective Christian song function is explicit.
exemplars: Salt of the Sound — Beyond Here
Salt of the Sound — Lent, Vol. 3
Salt of the Sound & Khamir Music — words unspoken

tradition.name: Argentine ambient
tradition.lineage: A geographically grouped ambient scene with multiple practices, including Leandro Fresco’s layered synthesizer compositions and Federico Durand’s intimate recorded loops and small sounds. This representative model combines quiet synth colour, a clean guitar fragment and looping recorded material; it does not assert a national timbre or compulsory tango instrumentation.

extras.description: Argentine ambient is a regional discovery category, not one inherited rhythmic form. Leandro Fresco’s El Reino Invisible documents slow synth textures and guitar details recorded between Buenos Aires and San Martín de los Andes; Federico Durand describes cassette collage, asymmetrical repetition, field recordings and modest sonic materials. The reduced default selects the synth/guitar/loop intersection while leaving their other methods editable. Unlike ambient_synth’s foregrounded arpeggio model, this branch gives diffuse melody and recorded fragments more space. Geography supports the catalogue grouping; it does not warrant adding folklore instruments, an Indigenous lineage or tango rhythm without entry-specific evidence.

entries.geo_rationale: Kompakt documents Fresco’s Buenos Aires formation and recording there; Durand’s own interview also discusses the metropolitan scene. The pin is one practice anchor, not an exclusive origin.

tradition.name: Australian ambient
tradition.lineage: Australian atmospheric electronic and electroacoustic practices, represented here by Lawrence English and the Brisbane ROOM40 network: environmental listening, recorded sound and slowly transformed electronic material. A representative field-recording/synthesis arrangement is selected rather than a national instrument inventory.

extras.description: Australian ambient groups a diverse scene by documented practice in Australia. The selected Lawrence English branch emphasizes field-recorded environments and their transformation: Ghost Towns is built largely from recorded sound treated with EQ and pitch shifting, and later collaborations credit electronics and environmental recordings. The sampler is a registered representation of recorded-material manipulation and the synth a quiet sustaining layer; neither is asserted as the hardware used on Ghost Towns. Compared with the melodic synth-and-guitar selection for Argentine ambient, this default gives listening texture and irregular environmental events greater weight. No pan-Australian timbre, automatic didgeridoo chair or Indigenous provenance is inferred.
exemplars: David Toop & Lawrence English — The Shell That Speaks the Sea (2023)

entries.geo_rationale: ROOM40 and English document Brisbane performance/label activity; the Commons photograph also identifies Brisbane. This is one established practice node in a diverse national scene.
